evidence: The current supplier page and all four A-page item bodies were inspected. In particular, def-bayesian-model-as-prior-and-sampling-kernel defines a proper model as a prior probability plus a parameter-measurable sampling probability kernel, while def-bayesian-posterior-as-regular-conditional-law distinguishes sample-point RCDs from data-indexed kernels. The batch-22 loss update uses only a supplied prior probability and fixed measurable loss; it makes no model or posterior-kernel claim. This records interface inspection, not independent approval.

The current BCS-02 definition and proposition were inspected, including the complete proposition proof. The definition treats a fixed nonnegative likelihood section against a sigma-finite measure; the proposition proves that a finite positive evidence normalizer is exactly the condition for a finite positive scaling to be a probability. It separately warns that pointwise likelihood sections do not assert joint measurability. Batch 22 defines a distinct fixed-observation loss weight exp(-w ell), requires its own finite positive normalizer, and does not identify the loss with a likelihood. This records interface inspection, not independent approval.
